subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The 'place' element of the marketing mix is mainly concerned with:
options: How and where the product reaches the customer
questions.explain: Place refers to the distribution channels and locations through which products reach customers.

questions.q: Retained profit is a popular source of finance for established businesses because it:
options: Has no interest cost and does not have to be repaid
Can only be used by plcs
Must be paid back within 30 days
questions.explain: Retained profit is internal, carries no interest and does not need repaying, making it a low-cost source of finance.

questions.q: A trade-off between ethics and profit occurs when:
options: Ethics and profit always rise together
Doing the most ethical thing reduces profit, forcing a choice
questions.explain: A trade-off means choosing the more ethical option may lower profit, so the business must balance the two.

questions.q: The 'boom' stage of the business cycle is usually marked by:
options: Falling demand and many business closures
High consumer spending, rising demand and growing output
questions.explain: In a boom, the economy grows strongly with high spending, rising demand and increasing output.

questions.q: High unemployment in the economy is likely to mean:
options: Lower consumer incomes and reduced demand for many products
Consumers have more money to spend
questions.explain: High unemployment lowers overall incomes and tends to reduce demand for many goods and services.

questions.q: Which item would appear as a cash inflow on a cash-flow forecast?
questions.explain: Cash received from sales is money coming into the business, so it is an inflow on a cash-flow forecast.

questions.q: Secondary market research involves:
options: Using data that already exists, such as published reports
questions.explain: Secondary research uses existing data such as government statistics or market reports.

questions.q: Why is good customer service important to a business?
options: It removes the need to sell products
It always lowers costs to zero
It can increase customer loyalty and repeat business
questions.explain: Good customer service encourages loyalty and repeat purchases, helping sales and reputation.

questions.q: Total costs are calculated by:
options: Adding fixed costs and variable costs
questions.explain: Total costs = fixed costs + variable costs.

questions.q: Reducing a business's environmental impact might involve:
options: Recycling, cutting waste and using renewable energy
questions.explain: Businesses reduce environmental impact through recycling, cutting waste and using cleaner energy.

questions.q: What is market segmentation?
options: Dividing a market into groups of customers with similar characteristics
questions.explain: Segmentation splits a market into groups (e.g. by age, income or lifestyle) so marketing can be targeted.

questions.q: On a bar gate stock control chart, the reorder level is the point at which:
options: A new order for stock should be placed
questions.explain: The reorder level is the stock level that triggers a new order, allowing for the supplier's lead time.

questions.q: If the exchange rate of the pound rises (strong pound), UK exports tend to become:
questions.explain: A stronger pound makes UK exports more expensive for overseas buyers, which can reduce export demand.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Profit and cash are the same thing
Customers may pay later while the business must pay its own bills now
Profit is always paid in cash immediately
questions.explain: Profit and cash differ in timing; a firm can be profitable yet short of cash if money comes in slowly.

questions.q: Public relations (PR) as a method of promotion mainly aims to:
options: Build and maintain a positive public image of the business
Reduce the size of the workforce
questions.explain: PR seeks to create a favourable public image, for example through press coverage or sponsorship.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an internal economy of scale?
options: A fall in industry-wide transport costs
A government grant to all firms
Purchasing economies from buying materials in bulk at a lower unit price
questions.explain: Bulk buying lowers the unit cost of materials, which is an internal (purchasing) economy of scale.

questions.q: A multinational company (MNC) is a business that:
options: Trades only in its home town
Operates and produces in more than one country
questions.explain: A multinational operates in several countries, often producing and selling across national borders.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an internal source of finance?
questions.explain: Retained profit is generated within the business, making it an internal source of finance.

questions.q: What is productivity?
options: The total amount of stock held
Output produced per unit of input (e.g. per worker) in a given time
questions.explain: Productivity measures output per input, such as the number of units produced per worker per hour.

questions.q: Inflation refers to:
options: A general rise in the price level over time
A rise in interest rates only
A fall in the number of workers
questions.explain: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general level of prices in an economy.

questions.q: Efficiency in operations means:
options: Producing output using the fewest resources and least waste
Hiring as many workers as possible
Always producing the cheapest possible product
questions.explain: Efficiency means getting the most output from the available inputs while minimising waste.

questions.q: Which of the following is total revenue?
options: Selling price multiplied by quantity sold
questions.explain: Total revenue = selling price x quantity sold.
